key_insight: HumanX compiles large-scale human video into reusable, agile interaction skills for humanoid robots, enabling generalizable real-world behaviors without per-task reward engineering.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap caused by scarce realistic interaction data and costly task-specific reward design, enabling scalable learning of adaptive humanoid interaction skills.
method: Full-stack pipeline that converts human videos into compact skill representations and supervision for robot policies (data curation → representation extraction → policy learning).
Reward-free learning: train interaction skills from imitation and self-supervision instead of hand-designed, task-specific rewards.
Sim-to-real and control adaptation: refine policies with simulation-aware dynamics and adaptive controllers for stable transfer to humanoid hardware.
impact: Reduces engineering overhead and unlocks scalable transfer of rich human behaviors to humanoid platforms, accelerating development of adaptive interactive robots for real-world tasks.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: human video → representation extractor → skill library → robot policy → real-world execution
Before/after success-rate chart: baseline methods vs HumanX across multiple interaction tasks

Sim-to-real illustration: policy trained in sim, adapted controller, and real humanoid executing the skill
paper_title: HumanX: Toward Agile and Generalizable Humanoid Interaction Skills from Human Videos
paper_authors: Yinhuai Wang, Qihan Zhao, Yuen Fui Lau, Runyi Yu, Hok Wai Tsui
